summary: Round 2 re-review of all 9 units. The round 1 fixes are present and consistent: FIGO 2018 IB1/IB2/IB3 boundaries (table, worked example, q006 key and explanation), GnRH analogues no longer called contraceptive (lesson, worked example, answer, q009 marking guide and explanation), ulipristal 5-day delay, DMPA not LARC with the 6 percent typical failure, hedged Abortion Act wording, doxycycline pregnancy caveat, tranexamic acid as treatment not prevention, and the PID regimen in the sexual-health unit. All numeric keys were recomputed and are correct (BMI 16.4, fibroid volume 73.3, PPV 19.6, RMI 450 and 3,060, discordance 25, MMR 73.1 and 48.4/39.5 percent, shock index 1.28, Pearl 2, cumulative 24.6, progesterone day 25, TMSC 28.8, fold change 8, 114 true positives). No tab or control characters, literal unicode escapes or object placeholders were found, and all six LaTeX strings use correctly escaped backslashes. Remaining problems: the 25 to 49 screening recall interval is probably now out of date, the PID regimen wording was fixed in only one of two places, and a few small clarity points. This is an AI review; the course still needs a subject-matter expert (clinician) before clinical reliance, and all regimens, thresholds and intervals should be checked against current FSRH, BASHH, NICE, NHS England and RCOG sources.

issues.problem: The lesson states routine recall 'every 3 years aged 25 to 49 and every 5 years aged 50 to 64' (given twice). My understanding, unverified here, is that NHS England extended the interval for hrHPV-negative women aged 25 to 49 to 5 years from mid-2025, so 3-yearly is probably outdated for England. The lesson does say 'check current NHSCSP policy', but it still states the old interval as fact.
issues.suggestedFix: Source check the current NHS England cervical screening recall policy. If confirmed, state that routine recall for hrHPV-negative women aged 25 to 64 is every 5 years in England (with shorter intervals only in defined situations, for example after treatment or for immunosuppressed women), and note nations differ. Remove the duplicated sentence.

issues.problem: The PID fix was applied only in the sexual-health unit. The pelvic-pain lesson still says 'intramuscular ceftriaxone plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days', which can be read as 14 days of IM ceftriaxone and conflicts with the clearer wording in sexual-health ('a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone, plus doxycycline and metronidazole, each given for 14 days').
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to: single-dose IM ceftriaxone (1 g) plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days (teaching example; check current BASHH guidance), matching the sexual-health unit.

issues.problem: Emergency contraception text: 'hormonal contraception must be delayed for 5 days (and started with extra precautions ... until the method is effective, to day 7 for most methods)'. 'to day 7' is ambiguous: extra precautions are needed for the usual number of days after starting the method (for example 7 days for most combined methods, 9 for the oestradiol valerate/dienogest pill, 2 for the progestogen-only pill), counted from the start, not from the ulipristal dose.
issues.suggestedFix: Say: start the method no sooner than 5 days after ulipristal, then use condoms or abstain for the usual number of days that method needs to become effective (check FSRH).

issues.problem: q008 asserts without hedge that under the Abortion Act 1967 in England and Wales two registered medical practitioners must certify. The lesson hedges the law ('check current law'), but this key and the unit summary state it as fixed. Recent UK reforms on the criminal liability of women for their own abortion, and the telemedical early medical abortion pathway, are not covered and I cannot verify their current status.
issues.suggestedFix: Source check the current legal position in England and Wales. Keep the key only if two-doctor certification and Ground C up to 24 weeks remain accurate for clinicians, and add 'as the Act currently stands (check current law)' to the stem or explanation.
